races.name: Follow Tote On X Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Taj Crown
runners_data.note: Prominent racer suited by Good ground (3 of 5 sim-going runs placed or close), drops in trip slightly from recent outings and wears a visor; W J Lee in the saddle for a yard with a modest recent strike-rate, but tracking Royal Approval from the outset is a natural fit for this horse's style.|

runners_data.name: Persian Bliss
runners_data.note: High-OR runner returning from 116 days off (64-day jumps layoff flag) with a tongue-strap applied; the long absence is the key concern, though the two good-ground runs in history include a placing and the 1m4f trip suits, making condition fitness the swing factor.|

runners_data.name: Royal Approval
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner and pace-setter for the race; a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 suggests this trip and prominent role may be slightly outside its optimal profile — five similar-going runs yielding no wins flags doubt — but the tactical advantage of a clear lead on Good ground here is concrete and significant.|

runners_data.name: Plontier
runners_data.note: W P Mullins's nine-year-old was off 282 days before this latest campaign entry; a genuine hold-up horse whose history shows reasonable good-ground finishes (4th in similar going last visit), and the strong yard gives hope of fitness, but the lack of recent racing is a real concern at this age.|

runners_data.name: Battling Siki
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type returning from 60 days with a prior headgear note (p flag); only one comparable good-ground run in the sample and the form figures show no placing yet, though Mark Fahey's 3/10 T14 rate suggests the yard has horses ready when they run.|

runners_data.name: Timandi
runners_data.note: Trainer has a 0/1 T14 record and the horse carries a REDISTRIBUTED flag — a true hold-up type that will not get to the rear where it wants to be, instead finding itself in midfield against its instincts with a STYLE_FIT of 0.90; five career runs show no win and the distance step up to 1m4f is new territory based on the history.|

runners_data.name: Stone Rulya
runners_data.note: Returning from 263 days (only 5 jumping days), this four-year-old carries a fade-in-finish warning alongside its REDISTRIBUTED flag, meaning it will be squeezed into midfield rather than its natural rear position and its tendency to weaken late compounds the disadvantage; Good-ground record of 5/9 comparable runs with no win is sobering.|

runners_data.name: Wolfpack
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's second string carries both a fade-in-finish flag and REDISTRIBUTED status — a true hold-up horse that will end up in midfield, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 and one win from 11 similar-going runs, the finishing kick required in this race shape is not naturally in its locker at Tramore today.|

races.paceDynamic: Royal Approval is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no identified rival likely to seriously press for the lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m4f trip on Good ground at Tramore. Taj Crown and Persian Bliss are the natural prominent types most likely to track Royal Approval into positions directly behind, giving the race a settled, strung-out shape from early on. This unhurried pace scenario strongly favours horses who can travel close to the leader and produce a decisive move approaching the final obstacles, meaning prominent-to-midfield closers with tactical speed — not true hold-up types forced wide and late — are the primary beneficiaries. This field carries more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate: Wolfpack, Stone Rulya, and Timandi are genuine rear-of-field types who are unlikely to secure their natural position and will instead find themselves shuffled into midfield against their instincts, diluting their finishing effectiveness.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Royal Approval Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Approval jumps cleanly, takes the rail, and controls a measured tempo with no serious challenger for the lead.
scenarios.body: Royal Approval sets a comfortable, controlled pace that keeps the race honest without burning off rivals prematurely, and the horses travelling closest — Taj Crown and Persian Bliss — get first run at the business end where a clean jump at the last is decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Outstay Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Taj Crown or Persian Bliss press Royal Approval from the second fence and a competitive early gallop develops.
scenarios.body: A slightly stronger pace drains Royal Approval's stamina reserves in the final furlong, allowing a prominent horse who has tracked economically to wear down the leader between the last two flights.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Midfield Closer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the field strings out, leaving those settled in midfield with cover and momentum to pick off tired rivals.
scenarios.body: Plontier, who has the experience and is the one genuine hold-up horse with credible good-ground form in the data, would be the primary beneficiary if stamina failures open a gap in the dying strides.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapses or Falls
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Approval makes a serious jumping error or stumbles early, removing the pace anchor and causing the field to bunch and contest the front.
scenarios.body: Without a controlling influence the race becomes a scramble for position, favouring any horse able to slot prominently off the reshuffle; Battling Siki's younger legs and headgear note give it an outside claim in this messy scenario.

watchPoints.text: Royal Approval's jumping must be monitored from the first fence — any mistake at the head of affairs immediately disrupts the controlled pace scenario that roughly 62% of the race probability rests upon.

Persian Bliss is 116 days off the track (64-day jumps layoff flag) and any sign of blowing hard or losing position after the early fences would signal fitness concerns that make its OR-85 class redundant.

Wolfpack, Stone Rulya, and Timandi are all flagged as fading finishers or REDISTRIBUTED hold-up types — if any of these three push forward aggressively from the gate in a bid for position, it would inject unexpected early pace and unsettle Royal Approval's control.

Plontier's layoff of 282 days means a first-time-out run for a nine-year-old should be treated cautiously, but W P Mullins runners returning off long breaks can be fit — watch for how sharply it is ridden out of the gate as a fitness indicator.

races.name: Waterford Castle And Resort Style Evening August 15th Maiden

runners_data.name: Big Dispute
runners_data.note: Form figures of 69 at shorter trips are unimpressive, though it has placed over staying trips on good ground before; a natural hold-up horse who will sit deeper than ideal in this moderate pace, making a winning effort hard to construct from off the bridle.

runners_data.name: Double Indian
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington runner carrying a warning flag for fading finishes, with only two runs to its name both on good ground and neither resulting in a placing; genuine hold-up preference means it is pushed into a position that does not suit in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: El Galvino
runners_data.note: 144 days off the track is a significant concern, and its Stanjames form on a very different surface is hard to translate to Tramore on good turf; inclined to come from off the pace but will find a crawling gallop set by Jetoile working against any late flourish.

runners_data.name: Half Cut
runners_data.note: Single run on record — 15th of 15 over 12f at Leopardstown on good ground — gives almost nothing to work with; tagged as fading in the finish and, as a hold-up type in a slowly-run race, has no obvious route into contention.

runners_data.name: Jetoile
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old veteran wearing tongue-tie, trained by W J Burke, who has won over 20f on good ground and knows how to control a race from the front; the key pace-setter here and Colin Keane's booking is the standout tactical appointment in the field.

runners_data.name: Way Down South
runners_data.note: Unraced for 38 days but has placed and won at distances up to 24f on soft, and a return to good ground at 1m4f may just be on the sharp side; nonetheless a confirmed prominent racer who travels well off a steady pace and represents one of the most natural fits to this race shape.

runners_data.name: Blue Nasturtium
runners_data.note: Debut runner for K J Condon — trainer has 1 winner from 10 runners in the past 14 days — carrying 130lbs and entirely unknown in terms of style and ability; the going is listed as Unknown and lightly raced tag adds to the uncertainty, making it a wildcard with genuine upside if gifted.

runners_data.name: Dream On Baby
runners_data.note: 271 days off the track is a major flag despite showing consistent placed form, including a win over 21f on good ground; wears a tongue-tie, trained by Emmet Mullins (2 winners from 11 recently), and as a legitimate prominent-type its style suits this race shape if fitness is not an issue after such a long layoff.

runners_data.name: Kimy
runners_data.note: Six days since last run, finished 7th after a previous 10th, and carries a fading-in-finish warning; hold-up profile is a poor match for a race run at Jetoile's tempo and the apprentice claim for Nicola Burns (5) does not provide sufficient compensation.

runners_data.name: Walls Cross
runners_data.note: Only career run was 10th of 10 over 12f at Navan on heavy ground, so going to good is an unknown and the Tramore step to 1m4f is uncharted territory; fades in the finish and, as a hold-up type making just its second start, has the longest odds against it in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Jetoile is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Colin Keane in the saddle, will stride on from the gate to control a steady, sustainable gallop over this 1m4f on good ground at Tramore. Way Down South and Dream On Baby are the only genuine prominent types to push up behind, meaning the early pace will be orderly and unhurried rather than contested. This creates a race shape that strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and quicken from a good position in the straight — hold-up horses relying on a strong end-to-end gallop to close will find the tempo insufficient. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can absorb: Big Dispute, Double Indian, El Galvino, Half Cut, Kimy, and Walls Cross all prefer coming from off the pace, but with Jetoile dictating a measured tempo, only those who adapt their position or get a favourable split will have any meaningful hope; Jetoile and the genuine prominent types are best placed to exploit a controlled pace from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jetoile Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Jetoile bowls along unchallenged and the pace remains measured throughout, allowing a prominent tracker to pounce in the straight.
scenarios.body: Jetoile sets an uncontested gallop and the race is run at a tempo that suits those travelling just behind, leaving the hold-up brigade with too little to run at in the closing stages. Way Down South and Dream On Baby, as genuine prominent types with decent staying form, are best positioned to take advantage of the controlled pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Jetoile Fades, Front Leads Home
scenarios.trigger: If Jetoile's stamina holds all the way to the line from an unchallenged lead on good ground over this trip.
scenarios.body: At 11 years old and wearing a tongue-tie, Jetoile has won over 20f in a similar vein and could simply stay on strongly if the gallop is moderate enough to keep reserves for the finish. The combination of uncontested lead and good ground plays directly to a front-runner who does not need to be pressed to find his rhythm.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types manages to get a better tactical position than expected and the pace quickens enough to suit a late run.
scenarios.body: Blue Nasturtium is an unknown quantity on debut for K J Condon and could emerge from the midfield pack with unexposed potential if the tempo lifts, while Big Dispute carries the best recent form figures in the field and could land a blow if Jetoile's pace is slightly more honest than expected. This scenario is discounted because the majority of hold-up horses are racing out of their preferred role and the controlled pace works against a late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Total Chaos, No Real Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Jetoile is sluggish from the gate or the field bunches and the race becomes a slow-run sprint, turning chaotic up the straight.
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly messy race with no true shape could produce a random result from anywhere in the field, with Big Dispute's class figures giving it an outside chance in a free-for-all. This is the least likely outcome given Jetoile's confirmed front-running profile and Keane's experienced handling.

watchPoints.text: Jetoile (Colin Keane) — watch the early stages to see whether Keane sends him straight to the front unchallenged; if Jetoile slots into an uncontested lead, the race shape is effectively set and the scenario probabilities shift sharply toward prominent types.

Dream On Baby — after 271 days off the track, watch how it moves in the paddock and whether Gary Carroll deploys it prominently from the gate; a prominent horse returning from a long absence is a fitness wildcard that could either run a huge race fresh or fade badly.

Blue Nasturtium — debut runner for K J Condon with completely unknown style; watch its drawn position and early behaviour out of the gate, as a surprise front-runner or a horse that travels naturally into the race could dramatically alter the shape.

Big Dispute — despite being repositioned in midfield on the map, its OR of 120 is tied for highest in the field; if the pace quickens unexpectedly in the final quarter-mile, watch whether Rory Cleary can find a gap from what will be a deeper position than ideal for this horse.

Way Down South — unraced 38 days and stepping back to good ground after soft-ground form; watch whether W J Lee settles it prominently in the first two or three and whether it travels with any fluency, as its position behind Jetoile early will be the clearest guide to its chance.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Kashel Spring
runners_data.note: Returning from a 268-day absence (which was itself after a 98-day break), she has reasonable course-going credentials but a form string of 81414 reads as inconsistently placed; the long layoff is the dominant concern here and Alan Casey's 7lb claim does not fully offset it.

runners_data.name: Sea Coral
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, which is a significant negative in a slowly-run race where the concluding stages will be crucial; her four-run form string shows ability to place at 1m2f on softer ground but she drops in at 1m4f here on good, and the fading tendency may be amplified by the extra distance.

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose natural style is displaced in this pace map — she has won and placed repeatedly on good ground over 1m2f and is dropping from 1m4f where she finished third last time, so the form is live, but W J Lee will need to find a prominent position she would not naturally seek if she is to overcome the slow-pace mismatch.

runners_data.name: Daboya
runners_data.note: The race pivot: sole front runner, ridden by Colin Keane, winner on good over 1m6f and on good over 1m4f last time out, with blinkers fitted and a STYLE_FIT note meaning she is racing slightly out of role by mapping as prominent rather than outright leader — but in practice she is the only one with a credible claim to lead throughout.

runners_data.name: Justenzia
runners_data.note: Has placed twice from five recent runs including two seconds over 1m and 1m1f on softer ground, but the 0W from those five and a poor seventh last time out (1m2f good) suggest she finds it difficult to get her head in front; her hold-up style is fully at odds with this pace shape, compounding doubts.

runners_data.name: La Dame Blanche
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with no win in her last five and a form string of 08-747 that reads as a horse who spots opportunities rather than takes them; positioned as a hold-up type but mapped to midfield, and on 1m3f good ground she finished fourth last time, which represents her best recent effort — she needs a truly run race she is unlikely to get here.

runners_data.name: Questionable
runners_data.note: Back after 299 days (second consecutive long break; prior gap was 93 days), and while she has one course-distance win on good, her redistribution from natural hold-up position and her 9554 recent form suggest she is unlikely to land this on return — the layoff is simply too long to trust blind.

races.paceDynamic: Daboya is the sole confirmed front runner and, with Colin Keane aboard, will stride out from the gates to set a controlled, sustainable gallop over Tramore's flat 1m4f trip on good ground — nobody in this field has the natural inclination or mandate to go with her, so she is likely to dictate entirely on her own terms. The remaining six runners are all hold-up or prominent types by instinct, meaning the pace is almost certain to be modest and Daboya's lead could be a significant one by halfway. This creates a race shape that strongly favours those able to travel close to the pace or make an early move, rather than those relying on a strong tempo to generate a meaningful finishing kick from deep. The field holds far more genuine hold-up horses than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Marmeladova, Justenzia, La Dame Blanche and Questionable are all true hold-up types redistributed to midfield, and in a slowly-run race they will not get the pace injection they need; of these, Marmeladova with her recent good-ground form and Justenzia with her recent placed efforts are the ones most likely to find a prominent position if they try to overcome their natural style. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers and those able to sit just off a slow pace and quicken over the final two furlongs are most advantaged; pure hold-up horses face a significant style mismatch.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Daboya Dictates, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Daboya goes unchallenged and the pace remains modest, she builds a lead that the hold-up-heavy field cannot bridge.
scenarios.body: Daboya sets every fraction under a confident Keane ride, and with no rival willing or able to match her, the deficit for the closers proves too great on a flat track that does not generate extreme finishes. Prominent types who can travel close enough to pressure her late are the main dangers, but her recent winning form over 1m6f on good ground suggests stamina is not an issue over 1m4f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Movers Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Daboya's early lead is smaller than expected and the pace is just quick enough to stretch her stamina, allowing a hold-up horse to close.
scenarios.body: A marginally stronger gallop — perhaps triggered by a prominent challenger pushing up — means Daboya's advantage is eroded in the final two furlongs as the closers find more room to work through. Marmeladova, with three placed efforts from seven runs on good ground and recent sharp form, is best placed among the genuine finishers to deliver a late challenge, though her redistribution from natural hold-up position is a material discount.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-tracking runner sits close enough to Daboya to strike turning for home before the hold-up horses can get involved.
scenarios.body: Sea Coral, despite fading tendencies flagged in her profile, has speed to hold a tracking position, and if she can find a cleaner passage she may collar Daboya on the turn. This shape suits runners with enough tactical speed to occupy second or third early and deliver a sustained challenge rather than a short burst, making any horse willing to race prominently dangerous.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Hold-Up Pack
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up types break unusually well and crowd the pace, creating a more contentious early tempo than expected.
scenarios.body: Should Marmeladova, Justenzia or Questionable push forward unexpectedly, the early pace quickens and the race becomes more end-to-end, opening a small window for a genuine closer to benefit. Kashel Spring, returning from 268 days off but with solid similar-going form at Tramore's trip range, would be the theoretical beneficiary, though her layoff and declining recent form string make this a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Daboya's sectionals early: if Keane allows her to stride out uncontested she could have three or four lengths on the field by halfway, at which point the hold-up-heavy rivals face an impossible task on a flat track with no pace injection to chase.

Marmeladova's position at the start: W J Lee may push her forward to counter the slow-pace problem, and if she gets into second or third early this changes the shape materially and makes her a much more credible finisher than her natural style suggests.

Sea Coral's tendency to fade: with the race likely to be run at a muddling gallop and the finish potentially attritional rather than a sprint, her flagged fading habit over 1m4f on good could see her drop out of contention from a seemingly promising position turning for home.

Kashel Spring's market moves: after 268 days off, any significant support for her in the betting window would indicate stable confidence that her homework has been pleasing — worth monitoring but not assuming.

Justenzia and La Dame Blanche are both trained in the Denis Gerard Hogan and Dermot Kilmartin camps respectively, both with modest recent form — if either shows unexpected early speed to track Daboya, the race shape becomes fractionally more contested than projected.

races.name: Tote Tramore Derby Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Brewel Hill
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a string of placed efforts on good ground at 10f; steps up to 1m4f here which could suit stamina-wise, but 282 days off the track is a significant concern for a flat-race type facing fit rivals.

runners_data.name: Chopsticks
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, cleared to dictate from the front with no natural challenger to his position; has form at 12f on good ground and should find this 1m4f trip within range, though his style-fit score (0.91) reflects he is stretching slightly beyond his natural comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Churchwarden
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse by profile but has placed form at up to 15f and good-ground experience; wears blinkers and Gary Carroll takes the ride for De Bromhead's in-form yard (T14: 9/36), making this one of the more interesting profiles to track just off the pace.

runners_data.name: Magna Gee Gee
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old hold-up type dropping in trip from recent 16f outings, with zero wins or places on comparable going; W J Lee is a strong booking but the formbook offers little encouragement on good ground.

runners_data.name: Vervain
runners_data.note: Tagged as fading in the finish and a true hold-up runner whose place in midfield on the pace map is a consequence of the field's hold-up congestion rather than natural positioning; has a win and two places on good ground but is 259 days off the track — that layoff for a 3-year-old in this company is a real question.

runners_data.name: Surviving Murmansk
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up specialist with a win at 16f on good ground; shown to the midfield on the map purely because the rear is oversubscribed, with natural position further back — 228 days off the track (38 days since a jumps run) calls fitness into question.

runners_data.name: Highway Sixty One
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old hold-up type with consistent placed efforts over 12f on good and standard, carrying the lightest competitive weight; shown in midfield on the map due to redistribution rather than natural inclination, and has no wins to date.

runners_data.name: Itsalonglongroad
runners_data.note: A 12-year-old veteran hold-up horse who wins at 16f on good ground; wears a visor and has place form at this trip, but redistribution to midfield masks the fact he is a thorough hold-up type who will be hunting for gaps late — age and a 65-day break (39 days since jumps) temper expectations.

runners_data.name: Plus Or Minus
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish and has softer-ground form (0-from-5 last five on good/similar); displayed on the pace map in midfield as a result of the hold-up excess in this field rather than any natural front-running tendency — the formbook on good turf is discouraging.

runners_data.name: Appian Way
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old who flags as fading in the finish; his best form has come over extreme distances (20-24f) and 1m4f may be too sharp, while 146 days off the track (32 days since a jumps run) adds further doubt — natural position is further back than the midfield placement shown.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Fara
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish and has a poor record on going this firm, with all recent form on soft/heavy and from 10f; the step up in trip and the switch to good ground both look problematic for this 4-year-old.

runners_data.name: Shakita
runners_data.note: Flags as fading in the finish; has attempted 16f on soft ground previously with modest results and now faces a flat good-ground test — shown in midfield due to redistribution but is a natural hold-up horse who will need a lot to go right in a compressed late charge.

runners_data.name: Jazz Forever
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish but has a second place at 13f on good ground and a visor is applied; ran just four days ago which raises a freshness concern, and trainer Flynn is in-form (T14: 1/13) — holds a realistic stalking position if the rider can slot in just behind Chopsticks early.

races.paceDynamic: Chopsticks is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no serious rivals for the lead, should bowl along at a comfortable, self-regulated gallop on good ground without anyone forcing the tempo. The field is deceptively packed with hold-up types — Vervain, Surviving Murmansk, Itsalonglongroad, Highway Sixty One, Plus Or Minus, Appian Way, Fantasy Fara and Shakita are all genuine come-from-behind horses, many of whom will be competing for the same ground in the final quarter-mile. This field holds considerably more hold-up and midfield types than the race shape can naturally accommodate, meaning Chopsticks is highly likely to control the early fractions undisturbed, with Jazz Forever and Churchwarden — both effective from just off the pace — likely to be among the horses closest in pursuit. A lone, uncontested front-runner setting a comfortable gallop on a flat track with a large group of closers bottlenecked behind strongly favours a horse that travels prominently or just off the pace, with enough stamina to repel the eventual surge — Chopsticks' unchallenged lead is the dominant tactical factor, and genuine hold-up horses face a difficult task if the pace is too moderate to string out the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Chopsticks Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Chopsticks is allowed to dictate a comfortable tempo with no pressure from rivals, setting sail from the front without ever being headed.
scenarios.body: Chopsticks travels within himself on the flat Tramore circuit, builds a buffer turning in, and the bunched hold-up horses cannot produce a decisive late sweep when the pace has been deliberately moderate throughout. A prominent racer who travels just off the gallop — such as Churchwarden or Jazz Forever — is best placed to latch onto the leader's rhythm and pounce if Chopsticks ties.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If Chopsticks sets enough of a true gallop to stretch the field, creating space for a well-positioned hold-up horse to reel in the leader inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace forces the field into single file, and a horse with a strong finish from mid-division can thread through to challenge — Surviving Murmansk and Itsalonglongroad, both proven at this kind of trip on good ground, would be the beneficiaries if they can secure a clear run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Aids Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Chopsticks goes too hard early in front, blows up in the straight, and a tightly-grouped chasing pack produces a winner from the rear.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up horses compressed into a small area, the closers who get the cleanest passage late will benefit most — Brewel Hill, proven on good ground at the trip, and Vervain, who has shown class when conditions suit, would both be live if traffic clears.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Scores
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is uneven and a horse tracking Chopsticks at close quarters steals a march turning for home before the hold-up horses can organise their challenge.
scenarios.body: Jazz Forever, fresh from a recent run and carrying a visor, could capitalise by sitting a length or two off the pace and kicking before the closers can wind up — at 1m4f on flat ground, the jump from third or fourth can be decisive if timed correctly.

watchPoints.text: Chopsticks — watch how quickly Paddy Harnett (5lb claimer) establishes position; if allowed to stride clear by two lengths or more before the first bend, the race is effectively his to control and no other runner has the natural profile to pressure him.

Jazz Forever — ran just four days ago and now runs in a visor; watch the parade ring and early running to see if the horse shows signs of fatigue, as a dull or flat start from this horse would remove the main credible challenger to Chopsticks from close range.

Churchwarden — De Bromhead's booking of Gary Carroll after a 57-day break is worth noting; if this horse travels fluently in third or fourth and begins to close the gap turning in, it would signal this is a live runner rather than a pipe-opener.

Vervain and Surviving Murmansk — both are true hold-up horses tagged with redistribution warnings and neither has run recently (259 and 228 days respectively); watch how far back they settle in running, as a wide draw or sluggish break could leave them with far too much to do against a front-runner setting a manageable gallop.

Highway Sixty One — the lightest competitive weight in the field at 129lbs; watch whether J M Sheridan attempts to push this 4-year-old forward from the gate to take advantage of the low burden, as any break from natural hold-up tactics could change the race dynamic slightly.

races.name: Tramoreraces.ie Handicap

runners_data.name: Soaring Sun
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in this field; Patrick Flynn's 5-year-old can dictate entirely unchallenged, though her recent form (form string 323-17, 53 days off) and zero wins or places from 8 runs on similar going is a notable negative behind the tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Showyoutheropes
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll partners this 4-year-old who has a strong Good-ground record (1W4P from 10 similar-going runs) and returns after 109 days off; a genuine hold-up horse whose late run depends entirely on the pace being fast enough to set up a meaningful closing move.

runners_data.name: Devine Genius
runners_data.note: Adam Browne-Souza (7lb claim) takes the ride on this hold-up type flagged for fading in the finish; recent form of 6/60-0 and only 4 places from 7 similar-going runs make it hard to be enthusiastic, particularly in a race where closers already face a structural disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Metamorphic
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's yard is in form (T14: 5/30) and the tongue-pin headgear could sharpen this hold-up type, but a record of 0W0P from 8 runs on similar going over a trip where it has repeatedly weakened (9th, 9th, 5th) limits confidence despite the trainer angle.

runners_data.name: Glendower
runners_data.note: Eoin Doyle's 5-year-old wears hood and tongue-tie and holds genuine Good-ground placed form (5 places from 15 runs), but is a true hold-up horse shuffled into midfield by the crowded rear — its best position is not available here, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) appropriately tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Guy's Girl
runners_data.note: W J Lee on a 4-year-old whose best recent effort was 3rd over 13f on Good; a natural hold-up horse that will likely be pushed forward by race circumstances, which is not her preferred mode — she has placed once in 8 similar-going runs and faces a tricky tactical puzzle.

runners_data.name: Eastern Blue Bird
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and is flagged for fading in the finish; an 0W0P record from 12 similar-going runs and a recent form line of 8890-0 makes this P A Fahy runner very hard to fancy regardless of how the race is run, and being forced off her natural rearward position only compounds the difficulty.

runners_data.name: Forlio
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is a major booking for Paul Flynn's 7-year-old, who wears a hood and has shown stamina over longer trips (3rd over 19f); a natural hold-up horse that the map pushes into midfield — Keane may take a more forward view and that positional flexibility, plus the jockey quality, makes this one of the more interesting hold-up cases.

runners_data.name: Miss Crinshawn
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides this Peter Fahey 4-year-old who has been placed at 2nd and 3rd over 10-13f on Good ground; though a natural hold-up runner, she holds genuine mid-distance form and Coen may elect to take a more prominent position, which suits the race shape and makes her one of the likeliest beneficiaries of the redistributed group.

runners_data.name: Oust
runners_data.note: Josh Halley's 3-year-old carries top weight (OR 72) and races with a prominent style that makes him the most natural partner for Soaring Sun at the head of affairs; his Good-ground form (2 places from 6 runs) and consistent placing record suggest he will be involved throughout, though giving weight all round is a real ask.

runners_data.name: A Pretty Penny
runners_data.note: Julian Pietropaolo (7lb claim) rides this Mrs Deborah Cody 3-year-old who actually has a win from 9 similar-going runs and was 4th over 10f on Good last time; a natural hold-up horse mapped to midfield by force of numbers, but the claim reduces her weight burden to 121lbs which partially offsets the positional disadvantage.

races.paceDynamic: Soaring Sun is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no genuine pace rival to push her, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. Oust is the only other horse with prominent tendencies and will likely slot in behind, giving Soaring Sun an uncontested lead into and around the Tramore circuit. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types, meaning the pace through the early and middle stages is likely to be moderate, placing a premium on horses that can travel prominently or make their effort from a handy position rather than having to produce a deep late run off a slow tempo. This shape strongly favours the front-running and prominent profiles — Soaring Sun and Oust are best placed tactically, while the many hold-up types face the dual problem of a slow early gallop compressing the race and too many rivals attempting the same late move. The field holds far more hold-up horses than can genuinely settle at the rear and produce a meaningful challenge; of the redistributed group, Miss Crinshawn, Guy's Girl and Forlio are the most likely to push forward and secure a more prominent pitch than their natural style suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Soaring Sun Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Soaring Sun is allowed to bowl along in front at her own pace with Oust tracking and no rival willing to apply early pressure.
scenarios.body: Soaring Sun sets a comfortable gallop that suits her stamina profile over 1m4f on Good ground, and the hold-up horses behind her are trapped in traffic hunting a winner who has never been truly tested at the front. Horses with prominent or handy positions benefit most as the lack of a strong pace means late finishers struggle to generate enough momentum to peg back the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Oust pushes Soaring Sun along through the middle stages and the pace becomes honest without turning truly fierce.
scenarios.body: A genuine tempo draws the race into a test of class and efficiency over the distance, suiting those who travel prominently and have the fitness to sustain their effort to the line. Oust, with the best OR in the field at 72, has the raw ability to pick Soaring Sun off if the pace is honest, with Miss Crinshawn and Guy's Girl also potentially in the mix having pushed forward from their natural hold-up roles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Handy Types
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the middle stages, creating a bunched race that triggers a sprint-style finish in the straight.
scenarios.body: A false-pace scenario compresses the field entering the home straight, briefly appearing to suit closers, but given so many hold-up horses are forced to race closer to the pace than ideal, the finishes converge and the runner with the best form in similar Good-ground 1m4f races gets up late. Showyoutheropes carries genuine Good-ground form credentials (1W4P in similar going) and would be best placed of the true hold-up horses if a late run is viable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clear Shape
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses dispute the front early, Soaring Sun is crowded out, and the race fragments with several mid-pack horses racing inconsistently.
scenarios.body: Disruption at the start or a faster-than-expected early pace causes the field to become strung out in unexpected positions, creating an unpredictable finish where finishing class and fitness override tactical advantage. This scenario is genuinely unlikely given the dominance of hold-up horses mapped to midfield, but Showyoutheropes and Forlio — with relevant Good-ground stamina form — would be among those with the tools to capitalise on a chaotic shape.

watchPoints.text: Soaring Sun could exploit unchallenged front-running to steal an unassailable lead if Oust and the remainder fail to organise themselves promptly out of the gates — watch for her to be allowed to bowl along in total isolation.

Forlio and Miss Crinshawn may both attempt to push forward early, creating a brief contested scenario for the prominent positions that could either unsettle Soaring Sun or paradoxically help her by drawing others wide and off the pace.

Showyoutheropes returns after 109 days off and Gary Carroll will need to judge the pace perfectly given a true hold-up run is only viable if the front end is setting a strong gallop — watch where Carroll positions him in the opening furlong.

With seven hold-up horses all seeking a position at the rear, Oust and any horse drawn widest may be forced to race in a pocket mid-race — traffic and switching room in the Tramore straight will be a factor worth monitoring at the business end.

A Pretty Penny's 7lb claim brings her down to 121lbs — the lightest weight in the race — which is a meaningful advantage if Ben Coen on Miss Crinshawn and Colin Keane on Forlio both elect to race more prominently and inadvertently set up a stronger pace than expected.

races.name: August Festival Early Bird Packages On tramoreraces.ie Handicap

runners_data.name: Voice Of Reason
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner mapping to lead here, but a career win rate of zero from six on good ground is a significant concern, and recent form figures of 225980 show consistent fade; Robbie Colgan takes over and the horse will set the pace but may not be able to sustain it to the line over the extra 2m trip.

runners_data.name: Carthusian
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher in the 6-11 range over this sort of trip on good ground, with headgear (visor) fitted and trainer Mrs John Harrington running at a solid 5/34 in the past 14 days; a naturally prominent-racing type who should get a position close to Voice Of Reason though the form figures on good going (0W1P from seven) are uninspiring.

runners_data.name: The Banger Doyle
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with a tidy recent record including a third over 15f on good ground, and Gary Carroll is a sharp jockey for a tactical race; sits naturally prominent which should be achievable here given the single pace-setter, though the step up in distance to 2m from recent 15f-16f runs needs to be survived.

runners_data.name: Matt Connor
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride on a hold-up horse that has won twice recently (1/10f and 1/18f), the 18f win on heavy being relevant stamina proof; returns from 90 days off (70 days since Keane last partnered), which is worth monitoring, but the style profile and quality jockey make this a horse to respect in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Liberated Light
runners_data.note: Back after a remarkable 858-day absence (38 days since jockey last rode), with a solid form profile showing a win at 16f on good and a second at 16f on good; Ben Coen is a top jockey who can handle a hold-up ride, and the tongue-strap is noted, though the enormous layoff introduces significant fitness doubt.

runners_data.name: Nelson Muntz
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type fitted with a hood and returning from 101 days off (39 days since jockey last partnered), with a best recent effort of third over 20f on soft; trainer David Harry Kelly is 2/3 in the past 14 days which is a sharp form angle, and this horse could benefit from a tactical race if it arrives fit.

runners_data.name: Mr Rango
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a course-relevant second over 17f on good ground in recent history; Siobhan Rutledge claims nothing here but the trainer has been quiet (0/14 in 14 days), and six of the last six runs have produced zero wins though the horse has placed — a place candidate rather than a likely winner.

runners_data.name: Inchiquin Maid
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 16f on standard at a different track, and Terence O'Brien fires a rare runner here; though a genuine prominent-racer by nature, the depth of prominent types in this field means she is likely to be shuffled wider or further back than ideal — the 146-day layoff between that win and today is also a question mark.

runners_data.name: Master Sydney
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by profile that has been mapped to midfield due to the volume of closers in the race — Paul Flynn is 0/15 in 14 days which is ice cold, and recent form of 04-060 offers little encouragement; the tongue-strap is noted but the combination of out-of-position mapping, cold trainer and modest recent form makes this difficult to recommend.

runners_data.name: Must Meet Cecil
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old visor-wearer whose recent form reads 860 and whose historical good-ground record shows finishes of 11th, 6th, 7th, 6th — consistently mid-division or worse; Rory Mulligan claims 5lb which helps the weight, but as a hold-up type displaced into a midfield map position and with no win from 12 runs on good ground, the profile is weak.

runners_data.name: Spanish John
runners_data.note: Won at 20f on heavy in earlier career and has placed twice over 20f on heavy ground, but goes well below that standard on good — eight runs on similar going bring zero wins and two places; W J Lee takes over from the regular jockey (23-day jockey gap), and as a natural prominent type being pushed into a midfield slot by the crowded shape, getting a clean run may be harder than the map suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Voice Of Reason is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 2m handicap and, with no genuine pace rival looking to press them from the outset, Robbie Colgan's mount should be able to dictate at a measured, sustainable gallop on good ground at Tramore. The field is congested with prominent-types — Spanish John, Inchiquin Maid, The Banger Doyle, Carthusian and Mr Rango all want to race forward — but because Voice Of Reason is the only one mapped to lead, several of those rivals will be forced to slot into a midfield berth they would not naturally choose, creating a bunched, tactical race behind the leader rather than a true test of stamina. With one horse controlling proceedings at an honest but unforced pace over 2m on good turf, the race shape is likely to produce a slowly-run first half and a sprint-style finish, which tilts the advantage firmly toward hold-up horses with a sharp turn of foot or prominent types who can improve into the straight without burning energy early. Tactical, well-positioned closers and any horse with residual speed that can produce a sustained run in the final quarter-mile will be at the head of affairs; true grinders who need a genuine test to show their stamina are disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Voice Of Reason sets a steady, uncontested pace and the field converges for a sprint-style finish in the straight.
scenarios.body: Voice Of Reason dictates every yard at a gentle tempo, keeping the race tactical, and the winner emerges from those positioned just behind who can quicken off a false pace; horses with good recent form at this trip and on good ground will flourish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Logjam Causes Trouble
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent-types — Spanish John, Carthusian, The Banger Doyle — jostle for position early and create scrimmaging that unsettles the pace.
scenarios.body: The disruption produces a more pressured first half than the lone pace-setter alone would generate, stretching the field and benefiting any horse that avoids trouble and travels smoothly in midfield; hold-up types that find daylight late could be rewarded.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses in the final half-mile and genuine hold-up runners produce a sweeping late challenge.
scenarios.body: With several redistributed prominent-types actually occupying midfield rather than racing in their true style, the genuine closers — Matt Connor and Liberated Light — could find the race set up perfectly for a late run; however the fact that Must Meet Cecil and Master Sydney are also not in their natural position limits confidence in a clean late swoop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Voice Of Reason is permitted to exploit the soft early gallop and builds a lead in the straight that no rival can close down.
scenarios.body: At 2m on good ground with zero pace pressure, a horse of genuine stamina settling into a rhythm can find reserves that a sprint-field cannot match; however Voice Of Reason's recent form figures of 225980 and the going record of 0 wins from 6 on similar ground make this the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Voice Of Reason sets the only confirmed pace and if Robbie Colgan goes too steady early, the field will bunch dangerously approaching the turn — watch for crowding among the prominent types (Spanish John, Carthusian, The Banger Doyle) as they fight for the positions closest to the leader.

Liberated Light returns from 858 days off and Ben Coen must judge fitness levels perfectly in a slowly-run race — if the mare is not race-fit, she could get outpaced when the sprint develops despite having the ability to win fresh.

Matt Connor has been off 90 days and Colin Keane has not partnered the horse for 70 days; watch the market moves on course as stable confidence in the return will be reflected in the price, given the quality of the jockey booking.

Nelson Muntz's trainer David Harry Kelly is 2/3 in the past 14 days — a hot short-term record worth noting in a race where the hold-up horse is returning from 101 days off and could be primed for the run.

Spanish John is a natural prominent racer pushed back to a midfield map position by the congested pace shape — if W J Lee elects to press forward regardless and take on Voice Of Reason for the lead, the entire pace dynamic changes and the race becomes materially faster than the solo-pace assessment suggests.

races.name: August Festival August 13th - 16th Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: He Who Dares
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who fades in the finish, returning from a lengthy 309-day absence which is a serious concern; the layoff combined with the confirmed fade flag makes it hard to trust him over 2m here even on suitable Going.

runners_data.name: Inchiquin Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with solid good-ground form across 16f trips, but stepping up to 2m after 299 days off is a big ask — needs a truly run race with a late pace collapse that may not materialise given the solo front-runner.

runners_data.name: Cala Gracioneta
runners_data.note: Hold-up fader who ran only 4 days ago and has limited turf-going experience, with her best form on Standard surfaces; the fade flag and switch to 2m over a course she hasn't faced are significant negatives.

runners_data.name: All In Peder
runners_data.note: True hold-up type with headgear (p) fitted, and a patchy recent record including 11th and 14th in 16f+ Good-ground races — the trip may be right but the form suggests he is well below the class levels needed to compete here.

runners_data.name: You Make Me Smile
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, though the STYLE_FIT tag (0.91) and headgear (v) indicate this prominent role is slightly outside her natural comfort zone; controls the pace entirely if left alone, but her best form has come tracking rather than leading.

runners_data.name: Takarengo
runners_data.note: Experienced 10-year-old whose natural inclination is to come from off the pace, but the field's crowded hold-up contingent means he will likely be pushed forward into a midfield berth that does not suit — T14 strike rate of 1/11 offers little trainer confidence here.

runners_data.name: Captain Hanley
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with headgear (ht) and a solid record placing at 24f and 20f on Good ground; Colin Keane's booking is the single most eye-catching positive in the race and he is well placed tactically if tracking the lone leader throughout.

runners_data.name: Black Soul
runners_data.note: Has a genuine tendency to come from the rear but the sheer volume of hold-up types in this field forces him into midfield, blunting his effectiveness; the fade flag and a 102-day absence compound the concerns for a horse rated just 49.

runners_data.name: Bynx
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with the most extensive Good-going record in the field (12/15 runs on similar ground) and a course win at 20f; the 27-day return is fine, and his tactical position behind You Make Me Smile gives him a straightforward path if his recent form (3-3-0-6-8) trends back upward.

runners_data.name: Reflectionist
runners_data.note: Returning from a staggering 1,518-day absence (over four years), and though trained by Gavin Cromwell who has a strong T14 strike rate (4/29), this is an enormous fitness question mark — as a natural hold-up horse bumped into midfield, the redistribution further compromises what little chance form suggests.

runners_data.name: Synchronize
runners_data.note: A hold-up type by nature who is mapped to midfield given the field's density of closers; the apprentice booking (7lb claimer Julian Pietropaolo) is a factor over 2m in a competitive handicap, and his form at this trip (10th over 19f) is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Lariat
runners_data.note: Prominent runner aged 10 with headgear (p), returning after 30 days and rated just 40 — has placed twice at 16f+ on Good but the raw numbers (0 wins in 15 similar-going runs) make it hard to build a case beyond being a safe pace-follower who completes.

races.paceDynamic: You Make Me Smile is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 2m handicap at Tramore on Good ground, and with no rival willing or able to seriously challenge for the lead, she is set to dictate at a sustainable, uncontested tempo throughout. Captain Hanley and Bynx are the two genuine prominent types who will look to track her closely in second and third, giving the race a defined shape from the front with a small lead group and a strung-out pack behind. The bulk of the field — He Who Dares, Inchiquin Star, All In Peder, Cala Gracioneta — are true hold-up horses who will settle in the rear half, but critically, Takarengo, Black Soul, Reflectionist, and Synchronize are also genuine hold-up types whose numbers exceed what the rear can accommodate, meaning several will be forced wider and more prominent than suits them. With one uncontested pace-setter able to control the tempo, suit herself through the bend and up the straight, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race in and around the lead or prominent position without expending excess energy — Captain Hanley and Bynx are best placed to capitalise, while deep closers face a stamina test rather than a pace collapse to exploit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Tempo, Front Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If You Make Me Smile dictates an uncontested, controlled pace and the hold-up brigade fail to get competitive momentum in the straight.
scenarios.body: You Make Me Smile rolls along in front at a steady clip, the pace never truly injecting urgency, and Captain Hanley or Bynx, tracking closely throughout, have enough left to pounce in the final furlong without needing a sprint finish to materialise. This shape rewards horses who travel prominently without getting into a speed duel, and the absence of any true pace challenger means the front two or three hold a decisive positional advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and You Make Me Smile tires in the final quarter-mile, leaving the race to the nearest trackers.
scenarios.body: Captain Hanley or Bynx, travelling smoothly just behind the leader, inherit the advantage as You Make Me Smile weakens approaching the final furlong, with neither having had to expend energy fighting for position. This scenario suits hold-up horses with proven stamina who have positioned themselves close enough to the action — Inchiquin Star and He Who Dares could pick up the pieces if they've crept into midfield with a clear run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses turning for home and a wall of tired horses opens a gap for genuine hold-up finishers coming from deep.
scenarios.body: He Who Dares or Inchiquin Star, both proven in this going, produce sustained finishes having sat in the rear, benefitting from a late fadeout among the prominent group. However, this scenario is inherently less likely given the displaced hold-up horses (Takarengo, Black Soul, Reflectionist, Synchronize) are not truly positioned to deliver late runs from the back — their redistributed placement undermines their ability to deliver a classic closer's finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If You Make Me Smile is crowded out early or the pace fragments with multiple horses disputing the lead from different parts of the field.
scenarios.body: A messy, stop-start gallop causes the race to bunch and a sprint develops in the final two furlongs, bypassing the stamina demands that should define a 2m contest on Good ground. Synchronize or Cala Gracioneta, both with turn-of-foot at shorter trips, could benefit from a falsely run race, though the weight of evidence here points strongly away from this scenario materialising.

watchPoints.text: You Make Me Smile must be monitored from the stalls — if she misses the break or is crowded by Captain Hanley and Bynx for the lead, the entire race shape fractures and the solo-pace scenario dissolves immediately.

Captain Hanley's jockey booking of Colin Keane elevates his danger significantly; watch whether he positions just behind You Make Me Smile from the outset, as that is the single most advantageous berth in the race.

Bynx has the best proven Good-ground record in the field across similar trips — if he travels smoothly into second or third early, his proximity to the leader gives him every chance to hit the front before the line.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Takarengo, Black Soul, Reflectionist, Synchronize) forced into midfield means there will be significant jostling for position in the middle of the pack in the opening half-mile — watch for interference or horses getting shuffled back against their will.
He Who Dares is returning from 309 days off for Seamie Curling, who has a modest T14 record (1/5) — an unexpectedly sharp run would be a significant market move to note in the minutes before the off.
